issue_context.title: Add a -Shuffle switch to Get-Random for convenient collection shuffling
issue_context.body:
# Summary of the new feature/enhancement

`Get-Random` currently requires you to specify a `-Count` argument in order to extract a random subset from an input collection.

Sometimes you want to _shuffle_ an input collection, i.e. to return _all_ input objects, in randomized order, and it would be nice to be able to express that intent directly, without having to provide a `-Count` (which may not even be known; you can work around that with `-Count ([int]::MaxValue)`, but that is awkward).

To that end, a new `-Shuffle` parameter could be introduced:

```powershell
# WISHFUL THINKING - sample output.
PS> 1..5 | Get-Random -Shuffle
4
2
5
3
1
comments: What should happen if one had set both `-Count` and `-Shuffle` parameters? Should the command return just <Count> random objects and ignore the `-Shuffle` switch or return the entire collection, in randomized order, despite the `-Count`? Another possible way is to throw an error, but I don't think it is a good solution.

I think the most elegant solution would simply be to put the -Shuffle parameter in a completely different parameter set, so that it can't be used with -Count, via the `Parameter` attribute:

```csharp
[Parameter(Mandatory = true, ParameterSetName = "ShuffleSet")]
public SwitchParameter Shuffle { get; set; }
```

Then when determining your code path you can use `switch (ParameterSetName)` to determine which code path to take. 🙂

:tada:This issue was addressed in #11093, which has now been successfully released as `v7.1.0-preview.2`.:tada:

Handy links:
* [Release Notes](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases/tag/v7.1.0-preview.2)

review_comments: I'm not sure about the last condition. Should we compare strings to check the `Shuffle` parameter is specified, or it would be better to check just the `Shuffle.IsPresent` property?
I think checking either should be sufficient, really, but for consistency's sake we should probably keep it to checking the parameter name.
